$comment: Vendored snapshot of the Vianova DS semantic roles this system shares. NOT a live dependency: no fetch, no package, no submodule. It is a committed constant with provenance, read only by test/shared-values.test.ts. Updating it is a deliberate, reviewed act — if a value here changes, a Vianova DS role changed and the artefact Figma library must be updated to match in the same PR.
$why: Cross-FILE Figma variable aliasing requires an Organization or Enterprise plan. The Vianova team is on Professional (verified 2026-10-01 via Figma whoami), so shared roles cannot alias the product DS library directly and are restated in the artefact file's own primitive tier. WITHIN-file aliasing does work on Professional, so the semantic tier aliases those primitives properly — that is pinned separately by test/alias-integrity.test.ts. This file is what makes the restatement checkable.
$sharedRolesNote: Declared HERE, in the repo — not parsed out of Figma variable descriptions. The contract belongs to the code, so a description edit in Figma cannot silently weaken it.

$divergence.$comment: On 2026-10-08 the artefact palette was realigned to vianova.io rather than the product DS: the primary moved from DS teal to the site navy, and the neutral ramp moved from zinc to gray. Five of the six shared-role bindings were severed by that change. They are recorded here rather than deleted, because a binding that vanishes without a trace is how a shared contract rots unnoticed. Restoring any of them means changing the Figma library, not this file.

severed.reason: artefact primary is now navy/900, the declared primary of vianova.io
the teal survives as SECONDARY but at a new artefact-specific step, not the DS primary

$divergence.openQuestion: Is the artefact system intended to track vianova.io or the product DS? Until that is ruled on, this guard covers only white and the two systems can drift freely. Raised 2026-10-13.
